items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: and Walter Bishop, and some of them are going to be on the show.

ctx.x: guys coming out of the schools and so forth but I think that management and the music business has taken another look at it and said — hmmm, people are starting to like jazz. All those commercials I hear, everything is jazz now you know. And it’s a money making situation and most of the kids have no idea, they’re not in touch with the culture. With Josh Redman and so forth, Josh never has the time to spend with some older players or to see the older players, because they’re already moved aside, because of money…

And they’re gone. Which is nice because it gives other people a chance to work off of their situations, but we don’t get to hear the great ones and what they were doing. Tomorrow or Saturday there’s a Sonny Rollins concert and he’s using, on the concert, his, a group of people who grew up in Harlem in a certain neighborhood. The only one, Art Taylor died, so he would ordinarily have been the drummer. But Percy Heath and he’s using Gil Coggins, one of the piano players that’s worked, what do they call themselves,…
